pairs: Ab Omnipotente non sunt abscondita tempora:
The times are not hidden from the Almighty;
They have driven away the donkey of orphans,
et abstulerunt pro pignore bovem viduæ.
and have taken the cow from the widow as collateral.
They have undermined the way of the poor,
and have pressed together the meek of the earth.
Alii quasi onagri in deserto egrediuntur ad opus suum:
Others, like wild asses in the desert, go forth to their work;
they obtain bread for their children.
They reap a field that is not their own,
et vineam ejus, quem vi oppresserint, vindemiant.
and they harvest a vineyard that they have taken by force.
indumenta tollentes, quibus non est operimentum in frigore:
having taken the clothing of those who have no covering in the cold;
these are wet with the mountain rain,
They have used violence to deprive orphans,
and they have robbed the poor common people.
From the naked and those who do not have enough clothing,
they have taken away sheaves of grain.
They take their midday rest among the stockpiles of those who,
though they have trodden the winepresses, suffer thirst.
they caused the men to groan and the spirit of the wounded to cry out,
et Deus inultum abire non patitur.
and so God does not allow this to go unpunished.
They have been rebellious against the light;
they have not known his ways,
nec reversi sunt per semitas ejus.
nor have they returned by his paths.
The killer of men rises at first light;
he executes the destitute and the poor, but,
per noctem vero erit quasi fur.
in truth, he is like a thief in the night.
The eye of the adulterer waits for darkness,
He passes through houses in the nighttime,
just as they had agreed among themselves in the daytime;
and they are ignorant of the light.
it is treated by them like the shadow of death;
et sic in tenebris quasi in luce ambulant.
and they walk in darkness, as if in light.
He is nimble on the surface of water.
maledicta sit pars ejus in terra,
His place on land is to be accursed.
May he not walk by way of the vineyards.
Ad nimium calorem transeat ab aquis nivium,
May he cross from the snowy waters to excessive heat,
et usque ad inferos peccatum illius.
and his sin, all the way to hell.
but instead be broken like an unfruitful tree.
Pavit enim sterilem quæ non parit,
For he has fed on the barren, who does not bear fruit,
and he has not done good to the widow.
He has pulled down the strong by his strength,
he will not have trust in his life.
God has given him a place for repentance,
et ille abutitur eo in superbiam:
and he abuses it with arrogance,
oculi autem ejus sunt in viis illius.
but his eyes are upon his ways.
They are lifted up for a little while,
and they will be brought low, just like all things,
and they will be taken away,
and, like the tops of the ears of grain, they will be crushed.
quis me potest arguere esse mentitum,
et ponere ante Deum verba mea?
who is able to prove to me that I have lied and to place my words before God?
